steps.instructions: Check whether: Other TEG 6s analyzers are communicating. Other devices on the same network segment are affected. TEG Manager or LIS is generally available. Expected outcome: A device-specific failure is separated from a broader server or network outage.

steps.title: 8. Verify Approved Communication Configuration
steps.instructions: Review visible network or interface settings against known-good documentation or another properly configured analyzer. Do not change IP, server, interface, or protected communication parameters without authorization. Expected outcome: No obvious configuration mismatch is identified, or an authorized configuration correction restores communication.

steps.title: 9. Perform End-to-End Verification
steps.instructions: After corrective action, verify the entire intended pathway: Test or approved verification data exists locally. Data reaches TEG Manager if applicable. Data reaches the LIS if applicable. Patient/order association remains correct. Expected outcome: Communication succeeds across the complete configured path. Troubleshooting can stop.

steps.title: 10. Escalate Unresolved Communication Failure
steps.instructions: If cabling, network port, server availability, and approved configuration are verified but communication remains unavailable, escalate to the appropriate Clinical Engineering, IT, LIS, or vendor support path. Expected outcome: The problem is transferred to the team responsible for the unresolved infrastructure, interface, or application layer.

CCR.Complaint: Laboratory staff reported that TEG 6s results were available locally but were not appearing in TEG Manager or the LIS.
CCR.Cause: Clinical Engineering found the analyzer Ethernet cable was not fully seated at the network connection.
CCR.Resolution: Reseated the network cable, verified restored connectivity and successful end-to-end result transmission, and returned the analyzer to normal service.

title: Haemonetics TEG 6s Viscoelastic Hemostasis Analyzer - Test Will Not Start, Aborts, or Produces No Result
description: Troubleshoots assay startup, aborted testing, missing results, cartridge, sample, software, power, and workflow conditions before service-level repair is considered.

steps.title: 1. Protect Patient Care and Confirm the Failure
steps.instructions: Do not rely on an analyzer that is aborting tests or failing to produce results when clinical decisions depend on timely coagulation data. Route testing to another verified analyzer or approved laboratory method as needed. Determine: Whether the test never begins. Whether it begins and aborts. Whether the run appears complete but no result is displayed. Whether all assays or only one cartridge type is affected. Whether the failure is intermittent or repeatable. Expected outcome: The failure pattern is clearly established.

steps.title: 2. Review the Displayed Message or Test Status
steps.instructions: Record the exact message, screen state, or stage at which the test stops. Do not paraphrase an error if exact wording is available. Expected outcome: A specific failure point is documented and can be correlated with later troubleshooting.

steps.title: 3. Verify Cartridge Condition and Seating
steps.instructions: Remove and inspect the cartridge for damage, contamination, incorrect type, or poor seating. Install an appropriate known-good cartridge. Expected outcome: The analyzer recognizes and accepts the known-good cartridge. If the test starts and completes normally, the cartridge was the likely external cause.

steps.title: 4. Verify Sample Condition and Loading
steps.instructions: Check that the specimen is suitable, adequate, and transferred correctly using approved laboratory practice. Look for: Insufficient specimen. Visible clotting. Bubbles. Leakage. Incomplete sample transfer. Expected outcome: The sample is appropriate and loads normally. Correct an evident sample issue before further analyzer troubleshooting.

steps.title: 5. Confirm Required Test Information Is Complete
steps.instructions: Verify that required test setup information has been entered or acquired correctly, including patient or specimen identification where applicable. Do not alter protected configuration settings solely to make the assay start. Expected outcome: No missing workflow information is preventing test initiation.

steps.title: 6. Verify Analyzer Power and Stability
steps.instructions: Confirm: Power connection is secure. Analyzer remains powered without flicker or restart. No unrelated system error is present. Startup completed normally. If appropriate, perform a controlled normal restart. Expected outcome: The analyzer reaches a stable ready condition.

steps.title: 7. Check for Software or Interface Delays
steps.instructions: If the analyzer appears responsive but a test will not progress, confirm the local interface is not frozen and that required screens respond normally. If result transfer is delayed but the analyzer itself shows a completed result, treat communication separately rather than assuming the assay failed. Expected outcome: Local analyzer operation and external result transmission are distinguished.

steps.title: 8. Repeat With a Known-Good Test Setup
steps.instructions: When laboratory policy permits, use an appropriate known-good cartridge and suitable verification material or specimen. Expected outcome: A complete test sequence progresses from cartridge recognition through result generation without aborting.

steps.title: 9. Verify Result Availability
steps.instructions: Confirm the completed result appears where expected on the analyzer. If local results are present but absent from LIS or TEG Manager, the analyzer test itself may be functioning and the problem should be handled as a communication issue. Expected outcome: The analyzer generates and displays a valid local result. If so, test-generation troubleshooting can stop.

steps.title: 10. Escalate Persistent Aborts or Missing Results
steps.instructions: If multiple appropriate cartridges and samples fail, or the analyzer repeatedly aborts without an external cause, remove it from service. Expected outcome: The analyzer is prevented from producing potentially unreliable clinical testing until qualified evaluation is completed.

CCR.Complaint: Laboratory staff reported that TEG 6s tests would begin but abort before producing a result.
CCR.Cause: Clinical Engineering found intermittent cartridge seating caused by debris in the accessible loading area.
CCR.Resolution: Cleaned the accessible cartridge area using approved practices, verified repeated successful cartridge recognition and test initiation, and returned the analyzer to service after functional verification.

helpfulDetails: LIS or TEG Manager result availability.

title: Haemonetics TEG 6s Viscoelastic Hemostasis Analyzer - Touchscreen, Software Freeze, or Startup Self-Test Failure
description: Troubleshoots unresponsive controls, frozen software, abnormal startup, and self-test failures using power, accessories, environment, and restart checks first.

steps.title: 1. Protect Patient Testing
steps.instructions: Do not troubleshoot an unstable or frozen analyzer while it is being relied on for patient testing. Move required coagulation testing to another verified analyzer or approved alternate method. Expected outcome: Patient testing continues independently of the affected analyzer.

steps.title: 2. Confirm the Exact Failure
steps.instructions: Determine whether: The touchscreen is completely unresponsive. Only part of the screen is unresponsive. The display is frozen. Software navigation stops responding. Startup does not complete. A self-test failure is displayed. Record the exact screen condition or message. Expected outcome: The failure is clearly characterized.

steps.title: 3. Check for External Touchscreen Obstruction
steps.instructions: Inspect the screen for: Liquid. Cleaning residue. Gloves or objects resting against it. Protective material interfering with touch. Physical damage. Clean and dry the screen using approved methods. Expected outcome: The touchscreen surface is clean, dry, and unobstructed. If normal response returns, troubleshooting can stop after verification.

steps.title: 4. Disconnect Nonessential External Accessories
steps.instructions: If permitted, disconnect nonessential externally connected USB or peripheral accessories that could be contributing to startup or software instability. Do not disconnect required infrastructure during active testing. Expected outcome: The analyzer starts or operates normally without the suspect accessory. If so, evaluate that accessory separately.

steps.title: 5. Verify AC Power
steps.instructions: Check: Power cord is fully seated. Outlet is functional. Plug and cord are undamaged. Power is stable. Use a known-good outlet or approved power check when needed. Expected outcome: Reliable AC power is confirmed.

steps.title: 6. Perform a Controlled Restart
steps.instructions: When no assay is active, perform a normal shutdown and restart using the intended controls. Avoid repeated rapid power cycling. Expected outcome: The analyzer completes startup and reaches a stable ready screen.

steps.title: 7. Observe Startup Behavior
steps.instructions: Watch for: Freeze at the same screen. Reboot loop. Delayed startup. Self-test message. Display abnormalities. Unexpected shutdown. Expected outcome: Startup completes normally without recurring error or freeze.

steps.title: 8. Verify Touchscreen Function Across the Interface
steps.instructions: After startup, test normal navigation across several screen areas without entering or changing protected settings. Expected outcome: Touch inputs are accurate and consistent across the required user interface.

steps.title: 9. Perform Functional Verification
steps.instructions: Confirm: Normal startup. Responsive touchscreen. Cartridge recognition. Ability to navigate the normal test setup sequence. No recurrent freeze or self-test failure. Use an approved non-patient verification process. Expected outcome: The analyzer remains stable and responsive through repeated basic operation. Troubleshooting can stop if all required verification passes.

steps.title: 10. Escalate Recurrent Freeze or Self-Test Failure
steps.instructions: If the analyzer repeatedly freezes, fails startup, or reports a recurring self-test failure, remove it from service. Expected outcome: The unreliable analyzer is prevented from use until qualified technical evaluation is completed.

CCR.Complaint: Laboratory staff reported that the TEG 6s touchscreen became unresponsive during setup and the analyzer appeared frozen.
CCR.Cause: Clinical Engineering found cleaning residue and moisture on the touchscreen surface, while the analyzer completed startup normally after the screen was cleaned and dried.
CCR.Resolution: Cleaned and dried the touchscreen using approved practices, verified normal touch response and stable operation through repeated navigation, and returned the analyzer to service.

title: Haemonetics TEG 6s Viscoelastic Hemostasis Analyzer - Unexpected Shutdown or Power Supply Failure
description: Troubleshoots loss of power, unexpected shutdown, intermittent operation, outlet, cord, connection, accessory, and environmental causes before internal power failure is suspected.

steps.title: 1. Protect Patient Testing and Preserve Results
steps.instructions: If the analyzer shuts down unexpectedly, do not continue using it for patient testing until reliable power is verified. Move clinically necessary testing to another verified analyzer or approved alternate workflow. Expected outcome: Patient testing is transferred away from an analyzer with unreliable power.

steps.title: 2. Confirm the Shutdown Pattern
steps.instructions: Determine whether: The analyzer will not power on. It powers on and immediately shuts down. Shutdown occurs randomly. Shutdown occurs when the cord or connector moves. Only one outlet is associated with the problem. The analyzer restarts by itself. Expected outcome: The power failure pattern is documented before components are disturbed.

steps.title: 3. Inspect the Power Cord and Plug
steps.instructions: Check externally for: Cuts. Fraying. Crushed insulation. Bent or damaged plug components. Loose connection. Signs of overheating or discoloration. Remove damaged power accessories from use. Expected outcome: The cord and plug are intact and securely connected. Replace an approved damaged detachable cord when appropriate and retest.

steps.title: 4. Verify the Wall Outlet
steps.instructions: Test the outlet using an approved method or move the analyzer to a known-good suitable outlet. If the branch circuit or receptacle is suspect, involve Facilities or the appropriate electrical support team. Expected outcome: Reliable facility power is confirmed. If the analyzer operates normally on another verified outlet, the analyzer may not be the cause.

steps.title: 5. Check the Analyzer Power Connection
steps.instructions: Verify the power connector is fully inserted and not loose. Gently inspect for excessive movement without stressing the connector. Expected outcome: The connection remains stable and the analyzer does not lose power when normally positioned.

steps.title: 6. Remove Nonessential External Accessories
steps.instructions: Disconnect nonessential external USB or other accessories if they can be safely removed and are not needed for the power-on test. Expected outcome: If the analyzer becomes stable with an accessory removed, evaluate the accessory separately.

steps.title: 7. Inspect the Environment
steps.instructions: Check for: Blocked ventilation. Excessive heat. Liquid spills. Condensation. Dust accumulation around accessible ventilation areas. Placement against surfaces that restrict airflow. Do not open the chassis for cleaning. Expected outcome: The analyzer is dry, adequately ventilated, and operating in a suitable environment.

steps.title: 8. Perform a Controlled Power-Up
steps.instructions: Connect the analyzer to a verified power source and perform a normal startup. Observe for: Stable power. Normal display. Complete startup. No odor, abnormal heat, or sound. No repeated restart. Expected outcome: The analyzer starts normally and remains powered.

steps.title: 9. Perform an Extended Functional Verification
steps.instructions: Allow the analyzer to remain powered through an appropriate observation period and approved functional checks. Verify: No spontaneous shutdown. Stable touchscreen operation. Cartridge recognition. Normal test setup. No power-related message or reboot. Expected outcome: Power remains stable through functional verification. Troubleshooting can stop if the original cause was external and all return-to-service requirements are satisfied.

steps.title: 10. Escalate Any Recurrent Power Instability
steps.instructions: Immediately remove the analyzer from service if it: Shuts down again. Emits an unusual odor. Becomes abnormally hot. Shows visible electrical damage. Has a loose or damaged power inlet. Cannot complete startup reliably. Expected outcome: The analyzer is prevented from clinical use until qualified bench evaluation confirms reliable operation.

CCR.Complaint: Laboratory staff reported that the TEG 6s unexpectedly shut down during routine operation and would intermittently lose power.
CCR.Cause: Clinical Engineering found the detachable power cord was loose at the analyzer and the connection would separate with normal equipment movement.
CCR.Resolution: Replaced the damaged detachable power cord with an approved known-good cord, verified stable startup and operation without further shutdowns, completed functional verification, and returned the analyzer to service.
